text:
The Marquis de Sade has reentered the erupting volcano

from which he had emerged,

with his beautiful hands still adorned with fringes,

his maiden’s eyes,

and that permanent reasoning of every-man-for-himself

so exclusively his.


But from the phosphorescent salon lit by lamps of entrails

he has never ceased to issue mysterious commands

that open a breach in the moral night.


Through that breach I see

the great creaking shadows, the old worn crust,

fading away

to let me love you

as the first man loved the first woman,

with complete freedom.


That freedom

through which fire itself has become man,

through which the Marquis de Sade defied the centuries

with his great abstract trees

and tragic acrobats

clinging to the thread of the Virgin of desire.

translation.title: The Marquis de Sade
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering of Breton, not recovered from the French original; the surreal syntax and charged images are preserved.
